mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher discount rates eroding future cash flows.
failure_condition: In high-interest-rate regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or the Fed cuts rates within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which tends to boost equity valuations and drive positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In periods of weak demand, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite the labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects resilient economic momentum and reduced recession risk.
failure_condition: INDPRO does not show persistent expansion for at least 6 months, or 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to anticipation of future rate hikes dampening equity valuations.
failure_condition: Inflation remains below 3% for 3 months or the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) followed by a rise in the 10-year Treasury yield (implied by FEDFUNDS) indicates tightening credit conditions, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >5% in a month and FEDFUNDS rises by >0.2% in the following month
failure_condition: No significant negative 60-day forward return occurs after such a housing/interest rate interaction pattern in at least 4 out of 5 occurrences.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment (UNRATE) and a sharp drop in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggest a softening labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as valuations adjust downward.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by >0.3pp while PAYEMS falls by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or the interaction pattern recurs without negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 4-week decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 50-week moving average predicts a regime shift toward economic weakness, resulting in a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: INDPRO does not show a sustained downward trend for 8 weeks or the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of rising Treasury yields (implied by FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) without a corresponding decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 2.5% over the same period
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS does not remain elevated for 3 months.
